implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player vertical paddles controlled by separate keys
implemented_requirements.evidence: paddle.py defines Paddle with side-specific controls (W/S for left, Up/Down for right) and handles input to move up/down while staying within screen bounds.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces between paddles and off top/bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: ball.py update() handles top/bottom collision, reverses Y speed, and _bounce_off_paddle() reflects the ball off paddles with angle calculation.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring when opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: ball.update() returns "left" or "right" when the ball exits the screen; Game.update() awards a point to the opposite side via Scoreboard.award_point().
settings.WINNING_SCORE = 5; Scoreboard.has_winner() checks against this threshold and Game transitions to STATE_GAME_OVER when reached.
After a point, Game.update() calls ball.reset() with appropriate serve direction and sets state to SERVING.
Game class manages states (serving, playing, game_over), handles SPACE to serve, R to restart, and runs the main loop in run().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Rendering of paddles, ball, scores, and game messages
implemented_requirements.evidence: draw() methods in Game, Paddle, Ball, and Scoreboard render all visual elements using pygame.

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete two‑player Pong game meeting all core requirements: controllable vertical paddles, ball physics with edge and paddle bounces, scoring on missed balls, a configurable winning score, and automatic ball reset after each point. The game loop, rendering, and input handling are all present, and the code appears syntactically correct and ready to run with pygame installed. No major functional gaps or blockers were found.
